classification.difficultyReason: Choose the applicable logarithm laws, distinguish a squared logarithm from the logarithm of a power, then solve the resulting equations and filter candidates using the original domains.

content.prompt: Solve the following logarithmic equations. Remember to check that your answer is valid!

answer.worked:
Both log arguments must be positive, so $x>1$.

$$\begin{align*}\log_2\big((x-1)(x+1)\big)&=3\\(x-1)(x+1)&=2^3\\x^2-1&=8\\x^2&=9\\x&=\pm3\end{align*}$$

Only $x=3$ satisfies $x>1$.

Both log arguments must be positive, so $x>8$.

$$\begin{align*}\log_{10}\left(\frac{x+1}{x-8}\right)&=1\\\frac{x+1}{x-8}&=10\\x+1&=10(x-8)\\x+1&=10x-80\\9x&=81\\x&=9\end{align*}$$

The solution $x=9$ satisfies $x>8$.

answer.worked:
Both log arguments must be positive, so $x>1$.

$$\begin{align*}\log_2(x-1)&=\log_2\big((x+1)^2\big)\\x-1&=(x+1)^2\\x-1&=x^2+2x+1\\x^2+x+2&=0\end{align*}$$

The discriminant is $1-4(1)(2)=-7$, so there are no real solutions.

answer.short:
$x=e$

The equation reduces to a perfect square in $\ln(x)$.
answer.worked:
The domain is $x>0$, so $\ln(x^2)=2\ln(x)$. Let $u=\ln(x)$.

$$\begin{align*}u^2-2u+1&=0\\(u-1)^2&=0\\u&=1\\\ln(x)&=1\\x&=e\end{align*}$$

The solution $x=e$ satisfies $x>0$.

answer.short:
$x=9$ or $x=27$

Substitute $u=\log_3(x)$ and factor the quadratic in $u$.
answer.worked:
The domain is $x>0$, so $\log_3(x^5)=5\log_3(x)$. Let $u=\log_3(x)$.

$$\begin{align*}u^2-5u&=-6\\u^2-5u+6&=0\\(u-2)(u-3)&=0\\u&=2\text{ or }3\end{align*}$$

Convert each logarithm value to exponential form.

$$\begin{align*}x&=3^2\text{ or }3^3\\x&=9\text{ or }27\end{align*}$$

Both solutions satisfy $x>0$.

All log arguments must be positive, so $x>1$.

$$\begin{align*}\ln\big((2x+4)(x-1)\big)&=\ln\big((x+1)^2\big)\\(2x+4)(x-1)&=(x+1)^2\\2x^2+2x-4&=x^2+2x+1\\x^2&=5\\x&=\pm\sqrt5\end{align*}$$

Only $x=\sqrt5$ satisfies $x>1$.
